title: Mistral Medium 3
hook: Mistral Medium 3 chased frontier-class quality at a fraction of the cost — 'medium is the new large' — aimed squarely at enterprise deployment.
key_points: Released May 2025 by French lab Mistral AI, balancing strong quality with low cost.
Mistral reported it matching most of a frontier model's quality at far lower price.
Built for enterprise: self-hostable on a few GPUs, with a 128K-token context window.
Customizable via continued pretraining, fine-tuning, and enterprise knowledge bases.
content_html: Mistral AI released Mistral Medium 3 in May 2025 with the tagline "medium is the new large," arguing that a carefully built mid-sized model could deliver most of the quality of a frontier model at a small fraction of the cost. The release targeted enterprises that need strong performance but also predictable economics and the option to self-host.
extra_html:
What's new

Mistral positioned Medium 3 as hitting at or above 90% of a leading competitor's benchmark quality while costing dramatically less per token. It supports a 128K-token context window and is designed for deployment flexibility: self-hosted on a modest number of GPUs or run in any cloud. It can be specialized through continued pretraining, fine-tuning, and integration with enterprise knowledge bases for domain-specific work.

Why it matters

Medium 3 is a clear example of the cost-efficiency frontier moving as fast as the capability frontier. For many production use cases, the relevant question is not "what is the single best model?" but "what is the cheapest model that is good enough?" — and a mid-sized model that approaches frontier quality at enterprise-friendly cost is exactly that bet.

related.title: Mistral 7B
related.hook: Mistral 7B outperforms much larger open models on most benchmarks - showing that architecture choices and data quality can stretch a 7B parameter budget a long way.

related.title: Mixtral of Experts
related.hook: Mixtral packs 8 experts per layer but routes each token through only 2, so you get the capacity of a ~47B model at the compute cost of a ~13B one - open weights included.
